concept.title: What a person must look at first
concept.shortdesc: The categories the draft flags for human review, and why.

conbody.p: The draft is a proposal. These categories need a person to decide: accept, rename, merge, split or drop. None of those decisions has been made.

ul.li: : Split support for unpaid family carers (groups, advice, carers assessments) from finding or living with a carer for care needs.
: Keep horse riding, carriage driving and equine therapy together and move the canoeing, sailing and regatta boundary items into a separate water sports group.
: It would split into help with shopping and errands, and shopping at particular shops such as thrift or gift shops.
: It would split into breastfeeding and infant feeding support, and wider antenatal, postnatal and parenting courses and online learning for parents.
: It would split into racket sports (tennis, badminton, table tennis, squash, pickleball) and general sports facilities and other sports such as cricket and gym use.
: It would split into everyday medication prompting and management support, and drug-treatment prescribing and drug information.
: It would split into cookery classes and cooking skills sessions, and practical help with preparing meals at home.
: It would split into taught courses, workshops and professional training on mental health, and self-help tools such as apps and information on coping.
: It would split into foot care (chiropody, podiatry, toenail treatment) and hair services (hairdressing, wigs, hair donation).
: It would split into borrowing from a library or lending library, and ordering or downloading resources and translated documents.
: It would split into health and clinical assessments (clinical, falls, behaviour, driving ability) and education or skills assessments (skills, study needs, initial assessment).
: Split into people who have offended or are in the criminal justice system, and victims of crime including hate crime.
: Split into stroke and brain injury survivors, and a separate group for people with speech, language or communication difficulties (stammer, English as a second language).
: Split into menopause and perimenopause support, and pelvic floor weakness at different life stages.
: Split into people registered with a GP in a given area or referral scheme, and NHS staff or workers.
: Split the professionals, parents and carers who work with or look after children and young people from the children and young people themselves.
: Split into individual volunteers and people wanting to volunteer, and a separate group for charities, community groups, social enterprises and other organisations.
: Split into people seeking housing or at risk of losing their home, and a separate group for landlords, property owners and residential properties or buildings.
: Split into professionals and practitioners who refer or support others, and a small set of unrelated roles such as executors or people seeking professional training.
: Split into 'registered with a GP in a named area' and 'NHS staff or patients of a named hospital'.
: Split into 'women-only or men-only services' and 'open to partners, friends or users of a centre's other services'.
: Split into 'lives in Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin or nearby areas' and 'dependants of staff at a named military base'.
: It would split into term-time-only sessions, and time-limited stays or attendance rules (about three months, pre- and post-release, one day only, ticket-only entry).
: It would split into no referral, diagnosis or membership needed (open access), and experience-level conditions such as beginners only or some previous experience assumed.
: Split into 'people who have experienced abuse, bereavement or similar events' and 'people for whom the service is not suitable because of trauma or crisis'.
: It would split into living alone or housebound and unable to travel, and conditions about being unable to access other services or exclusions (not homeless, no immediate needs).
